source.title: Feature Hedging: Correlated Features Break Narrow Sparse Autoencoders
source.authors: David Chanin; Tomás Dulka; Adrià Garriga-Alonso

page_placements.theme: Feature hedging: narrow or too-sparse SAEs mix correlated features into latents

record.tranche_reason: The study proposes feature hedging as a distinct failure mode related to, but different from, feature splitting and absorption. It measures how hedging changes with SAE width and reports a feature-splitting metric under different Matryoshka loss settings.
record.gate_note: The main width-sweep and toy-model results measure feature hedging, not whether finer features partition a coarse feature's inputs. Those findings are recorded under fits_no_version. The study also reports a SAEBench feature-splitting metric across Matryoshka loss multipliers, which bears on V6. Values available only in plots are recorded as figure only. Cited findings from other work are not recorded.
record.test_reason: The study's own toy results show absorption arising from SAE training on hierarchical features and its dependence on width (V4). Its Gemma-2-2b balance-Matryoshka sweep reports how an objective change alters the SAEBench feature-splitting metric (V6). The main LLM results measure hedging, a different construct, and are recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors also state that absorption worsens as SAEs widen while hedging worsens as they narrow, so width is not a neutral hyperparameter. They suspect hedging partly explains SAEs underperforming supervised baselines.
record.recipe_differences: Uses SAE training on model activations and varies dictionary width, but focuses on a newly defined hedging-degree measurement and separate absorption/SAEBench evaluations rather than measuring whether larger dictionaries partition a smaller feature's inputs.
record.method_sensitivity: Hedging changes with SAE width and feature correlation; its sign tracks correlation. L1 penalty can reduce positive hedging in some settings but does not solve the anti-correlated single-latent case. Matryoshka loss multiplier changes the reported feature-splitting metric.

fits_no_version.finding: In toy models, hedging appears when correlated or hierarchical features exceed SAE width. Its sign tracks the correlation, and full-width SAEs recover the true correlated features. Loss curves show the MSE minimum lies at a mixed latent.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Narrow SAEs trained with reconstruction loss mix components of correlated features into latents (feature hedging), and widening removes this in toy models.

fits_no_version.finding: In Gemma-2-2b and Llama-3.2-1b SAEs, hedging degree falls sharply with width but stays above zero at 65536. L0 and layer have minor effects, and BatchTopK SAEs hedge more than L1 SAEs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Measured hedging in LLM SAEs decreases with width but is not eliminated at 65k latents.

record.problems: The authors state that they test hedging in LLM SAEs only up to 65k latents and on models with 2b parameters because of compute constraints. The width-sweep results are plotted without numerical values in the text. The real-model hedging measure relies on continued SAE training after adding latents; the paper also notes that the number of added latents is a hyperparameter.
record.rows_left_out: The paper reports additional hedging-degree sweeps by layer and L0 (Figure 8b-c), a sweep over the number of added latents (Figure 13), and other Matryoshka evaluation metrics (Figures 10 and 18). These do not directly measure the claim versions beyond the feature-splitting metric retained in R10 and the hierarchical absorption result in R2.

untested.parts: Whether larger dictionaries replace a coarse latent with finer latents that cover its inputs and lie near its direction. Not measured.
Splitting in large models or open SAE releases. The LLM experiments (Gemma-2-2b, Llama-3.2-1b, up to 65k latents) measure hedging, not splitting.
Nested, geometrically close feature families mirroring a concept hierarchy. Only one anecdotal case study (CSS/rel latent) is reported, and it concerns hedging.
Sparsity/L0 effects on absorption in real-model SAEs. Width effects on absorption in LLM SAEs are asserted, not measured here.
Decomposition of larger-SAE latents into smaller-SAE latents, and novel latents. Not tested.
Whether splitting says little about the model's own units in real LLMs. Only the SAEBench splitting metric across Matryoshka multipliers is shown.

missing.what: SAEBench mean absorption rate vs balance-Matryoshka multiplier. Matryoshka lowers absorption, and 0.75 'still scores well'.
Toy balance Matryoshka: β=∞ gives hedging, β=0 gives absorption, β=0.25 is near-perfect.
Toy unbalanceable case (child probabilities 0.02/0.2/0.5, β=0.17): slight absorption and hedging remain.

record.verdict_notes: R2's absorption pattern is a toy result described in the text, not a quantified rate. The paper's statement that absorption gets worse with width is asserted from prior work, not measured here. The splitting metric in R10 is SAEBench's first-letter-task splitting count. Lower is better per the paper.

versions.untested_parts: Whether a coarse feature is replaced by several finer features that partition its inputs and lie near its direction.
Whether that splitting pattern holds in large models and open SAE releases.
Whether split features form nested, geometrically close families mirroring a concept hierarchy.

The general claim that changing SAE size or sparsity does not fix absorption; the paper compares toy SAE widths and Matryoshka loss balances, not a broad size or sparsity intervention on real-model absorption.
Whether larger-SAE latents decompose into combinations of smaller-SAE latents and whether larger SAEs add novel latents.

Whether feature splitting generally says little about model units, and whether its observed pattern is caused by the SAE objective rather than the model's representations. The paper tests hedging as an objective-related phenomenon and reports a feature-splitting metric under Matryoshka loss settings.

relation.reason: Its own toy and LLM results bear on V4 and V6.

tranche.reason: Argues absorption and width interact with a second failure (hedging), so the narrowing remedy needs restating, and shows that a balance-Matryoshka objective can cancel absorption. Same-author work as the original.

source_check.notes: Shares authors with the Chanin absorption original. Main LLM results measure hedging, not splitting. Balance-Matryoshka LLM results are figure-only. Fig 10f '(SAEBench absorption)' names the eval suite, not a mislabel. Fig 3 caption typo: f3 implies f4 (text: f4 implies f3).

statements.correction: Beta 0 (standard SAE): absorption; beta infinity (detached): hedging; beta 0.25: near-perfect. Children at 0.02/0.2/0.5 with beta 0.17: slight absorption of f2 and slight hedging of f4 in latent 1.
statements.problem: Minor omission: at beta 0.17 the text also reports slight hedging of f4 in latent 1. Toy is in Sec 5 / Appendix A.7-A.8 (Fig 9, Fig 17).

statements.correction: R10: Gemma-2-2b layer 12, BatchTopK k=40, width 32768, 10 seeds. A balance multiplier of about 0.75 gives a better (lower) SAEBench feature-splitting score than standard Matryoshka (1) or standard SAE (0). Values are figure-only. The result is already described in V6.method_sensitivity[1].
statements.problem: Cites this study's R10 as support for the first-letter Matryoshka-vs-BatchTopK gap but never describes it. This study's text does not state that standard Matryoshka beats standard BatchTopK on splitting. It says only that a multiplier of about 0.75 beats both.
Slight paraphrase: text says about 0.75 beats standard Matryoshka and standard SAE on feature splitting (lower is better). Whether it is best across the whole 0-5 sweep is figure-only.

statements.correction: Full-width toy SAEs recover the true features for correlated and anti-correlated features (Fig 4, Fig 5 right, A.2). For hierarchical features the full-width SAE shows absorption (Fig 3 right). Independent features: correct at any width (Fig 2). LLM part correct: hedging falls with width, stays >0 at 65536; L0 and layer have minor effects; BatchTopK hedges more than L1.
statements.problem: 'Full-width SAEs recover the true features' is wrong for the hierarchical toy. There the full-width SAE shows absorption (Fig 3 right), not true features.
